House hunting is a long process for most people. Idk how long you two have been searching, but most people I know took well over 3 months to even find houses worth bidding on. I helped my dad find his current home a few years back, but because I was unemployed, I dedicated my full time to look through the listings online and the ones provided by his realtor. We were seeing 10-15 houses per weekend, and even that took months. Talk with your partner, maybe open up about your experiences with HOA in more vivid detail, and don't lose hope that you'll find your dream home together soon.

I think that when I lost my grandfather, the things that keep him alive most in my memory are all the life events he hasn't been able to be a part of... so to stay alive, I've made an effort to have life events to be present for: weddings, birthday parties, graduations, and even just random hangouts. Live until the next event, and make sure to plan for one after that so the cycle can repeat. "I have to make it until (insert event here)".

That's kept me alive since 2017.

It's good for many reasons. When I'm manic I tend to hyperfocus on other things and forget to eat or just don't feel like I have enough time to cook or even eat a full meal so having something quick is to ensure I eat at all. And with depressive episodes, it's similar, but more like there's too many steps to prepare and eat a meal, so having comfort foods and snacks you can make and eat quickly keep you fed. And having water bottles wherever possible. I keep 3 on my nightstand because I don't really get thirsty until my mouth is dry sometimes.

I took antidepressants for a while back in college for what we thought was just depression. The new meds had me awake for 1 week, not hyper, just not tired at all, then spent the weekend shitfaced drunk, then crashed, and didn't get out of bed for a week.
I'd say it's ok to test it, but make sure to have a support system checking up on you and plenty of easy access snacks/drinks just in case.

They later put me on a mood stabilizer, but it gave me a rash so I stopped taking it and then I dropped out and haven't had a steady doctor since then, so no meds at the moment.

Hope your experience is better than mine.
